tweets.text:
This is one of the better litmus tests for whether you’re pushing your use of AI enough or not. 

Up until maybe six months ago probably the best you could do with AI was pull off something you already would produce, but just doing it a little faster. But now we’re entering a point where the output of working with AI can and should dramatically exceed what you would been able to do before, in a fraction of the time.

The product prototype should not only be fully functional and interactive, but it should probably have meaningfully better features than it would have had before. The engineering architecture should be able to deliver performance gains that you wouldn’t have been able to go after otherwise. 

The research for a project should consume every single fact on the subject across every dimension of analysis possible. The business process you implement with AI should operate entirely differently and learn from all its past failures in a way no human could. 

We’re unquestionably entering a period where AI will be smarter than us on most axes. Perhaps not on every dimension that matters (intelligence is still very jagged), but at least on enough dimensions that when we combine it with what we’re good at, you get qualitatively different outcomes.

So the simple test is: if you could have done what you’re doing before AI, you’re likely not pushing it enough.

My goal with @cfosilvia is to build the best piece of software for serious investors who want to control their own money.

The big idea is that AI technology can help these investors navigate the complexities of managing their household finances, especially when it comes to tax, estate planning, investment decisions, and generational wealth transfer. 

Anyone can sign up, connect their financial accounts, and begin talking to Silvia about their finances. The more context you give her, the more helpful she can be. 

My initial suggestion for every user is to connect your accounts and then ask Silvia to interview you, so she gets relevant information that will make her even better at her job. 

Today we have over 20,000 investors and more than $60 billion in assets connected to the platform. The average user is a multi-millionaire and paying users ask Silvia 20+ questions per week. 

Given the product touches personal financial data, it has been important to me since day one that we embrace three core ideas of privacy, security, and accuracy. 

For example, we applied for SOC II certification when there was literally only me and @shaincodes at the company. Almost no one does that, but the privacy and security of our users is front-and-center for us.

Additionally, we have spent the last ~ 6 months rebuilding the AI tech stack to reduce our dependency on frontier models. This has allowed us to improve the accuracy of Silvia's answers on important personal finance topics like tax, mortgage, and credit cards. 

If you search the internet or here on X, you will find tons of people who love the product. They are tired of the amateurish budgeting and saving apps. These individual investors need a product that can help them grow their assets and net worth, not save $5 on Starbucks.

We are proud of the product we have built and think there is tons of room for improvement too. Our team is currently only ~ 10 full-time employees, so we are rapidly shipping new features and products with the hopes of delivering on Silvia's core promise to help serious investors accelerate their net worth growth.

If this approach resonates with you, I would appreciate it if you took a few minutes to sign up for the product and gave it a try. It is free to use when you get started and you only have to pay if you become a power user. 

Try Silvia: https://t.co/bMI7hLeK8s 

Feedback is a gift, so once you have tried the product, please send any ideas on how we could improve it. No idea is too small or too silly. We can only build the best product if we have smart users who share their ideas. 

I appreciate you reading this far and hope you enjoy using Silvia. We are having a blast building it.

纽交所母公司 ICE 删帖又重发，https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 合作并未取消，但这次明显多了监管前提。

ICE 最新公告确认，计划将 https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 基于 Hyperliquid 的永续合约引入美国市场，覆盖加密资产、股票、指数、大宗商品和外汇。

但与此前公告相比，新增了两个关键限定：「计划引入」和「须经监管批准」。

如果获批，ICE 将负责运营 https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 的美国受监管版本，用户通过美国监管的期货佣金商（FCM）访问平台，并接受 KYC/AML 审核。新交易场所将独立于 ICE 现有机构期货业务。

这意味着 ICE 并非简单地把 Hyperliquid 搬进美国，而是希望借助自身监管体系和 https://t.co/EMdUCKN9eM 的技术经验，将链上永续合约接入美国合规交易市场。

此前 ICE 删除原帖，一度引发市场对合作取消的猜测。如今重新发布并补充监管条件，更像是法务团队对公告措辞进行了谨慎调整。

真正值得关注的是：如果这项计划最终落地，Hyperliquid 的技术与流动性生态，或将通过 ICE 这样的传统金融基础设施进入美国市场。

传统交易所正在拥抱链上永续合约，但监管审批才是真正的门槛。

美股正在给 AI 狂热重新定价。

Alphabet 财报后股价一度暴跌近 12%，市值蒸发近 5000 亿美元；英特尔更是单日暴跌 28.58%，创下 1970 年代以来最差单日表现，美国政府持有的英特尔股份一天浮亏约 120 亿美元。

但这两家公司面临的问题并不相同。

Alphabet 的问题是：营收仍在高速增长，但市场开始担心 AI 基础设施投入过大，盈利能力和自由现金流能否跟上。AI 业务的增长故事还在，但投资者不再愿意只为增长买单。

英特尔则是另一种困境：PC 市场复苏不及预期，第四季度营收指引仅 150 亿至 160 亿美元，低于市场预期的 171 亿美元，调整后每股收益也只有 0.25 美元，远低于预期的 0.43 美元。再叠加以色列晶圆厂事故带来的供应链冲击，基本面压力进一步放大。

一个是 AI 投入太大，市场开始追问回报；一个是传统业务承压，转型仍未兑现。

这其实反映了当前美股最重要的变化：

市场不再为 AI 故事无条件买单，而是开始要求每一美元资本开支都拿出相应的回报。

过去，AI 投资规模越大，越容易获得估值溢价；现在，投入越大，反而越需要证明自己能够赚钱。

AI 长期趋势或许没有改变，但美股的估值逻辑正在改变。下一阶段，市场可能不再奖励谁最敢烧钱，而是奖励谁能真正把 AI 变成利润。

加密市场可能已经先于美股见顶，但也可能先于美股触底。

加密交易员 Ansem 提出一个值得关注的判断：本轮周期中，AI 与美股行情对市场风险偏好的影响越来越大，BTC 与美股未必会同步见顶、见底。

如果近期 BTC 的反弹只是逆势反弹，而美股才刚刚开始更大规模的调整，那么加密市场可能还没有走完下跌行情。

但另一种可能是，即使美股和加密市场短期继续下跌，BTC 也可能率先触底。

这意味着，不能简单用美股走势判断 BTC 的底部。接下来真正值得关注的，是两类资产接近关键价位时，谁先出现止跌信号。

美股未必是 BTC 的领先指标，BTC 也可能先于美股完成筑底。

今天是比特币白皮书发布 18 周年。

18年前，中本聪在密码学邮件列表里悄悄按下了发送键，一份只有 9 页的 PDF，开启了一场对抗传统金融的狂热实验。

一个人，这辈子能有几个18年呢？

这18年里，有人第一眼就看懂了，有人骂了三年才回头，有人一直到现在还在观望...

机会来过好几次，有人接住了，有人接不住，还有人根本没看见它来过。

浮浮沉沉十八载，熙熙攘攘万千人。

跳出这个圈子来看，人生的路其实也一样。

风高浪急，人言可畏；而年岁渐长，我们都必须找到一个属于自己的抓手，确信自己看好的人与事。

正如中本聪当年的名言：

"If you don't believe me or don't get it, I don't have time to try to convince you, sorry."
（如果你不相信我，抱歉我没时间说服你）

希望大家都能在自己人生笃定的事情上热烈的一意孤行，无惧流言蜚语。

今年还没过完，币圈已经记录了 322 起攻击事件，是去年全年的 2.18 倍。

大家的注意力被几笔天价盗窃案吸走了，但如果把 AI 的发展和被盗趋势一起看，很容易看到更深的问题。

2 月 5 日，GPT-5.3-Codex 与 Claude Opus 4.6 同日发布，找漏洞、执行复杂编程任务的能力进一步提升。

随后，加密行业面临的代码漏洞类攻击从 2 月的 9 起，升到 3 月的 22 起，8 月更是达到 43 起。

时间上的接近，让 AI 成了一个值得追问的变量。

更耐人寻味的是，增长最快的是小金额攻击。

据 Village 对 DefiLlama 数据的分析，今年截至 10 月 19 日，损失不足 100 万美元的代码漏洞攻击，已经达到历史同期平均水平的约三倍。

这很符合一种令人不安的变化：

当找漏洞越来越便宜，过去不值得黑客花时间的小项目，也开始值得被反复扫描。

攻击者未必需要攻破更难的目标，只要能用更低的成本，多找出几个没修好的漏洞。

AI 能帮开发者更快地写出代码，也能帮攻击者更快地检查代码。对加密项目来说，如果还保持以前的安全审计态度和频率，那就会越来越跟不上黑客叠加 AI 杠杆的速度了。

i've been thinking about the possibility that crypto topped before equities this cycle

if the recent bounce is just a countertrend move and stocks are only now beginning a larger correction, crypto could still have another leg lower

i'm not fully convinced that's the scenario we're heading into, but i think it's worth considering given how much AI and equities have driven risk appetite this cycle

Bitcoin could also find its bottom before the broader equity market does, even if both continue selling off in the near term

i'm keeping an open mind and watching how price reacts as these markets approach important levels

time is an underrated part of risk management when trading lower timeframes

when i enter a trade expecting a sharp move, i want price to react relatively quickly

if Bitcoin is sitting around my entry for too long without moving in the direction i expected, i start questioning the setup

the advantage of trading lower timeframes is that you can recognize when something isn't working much earlier

sometimes i'll exit a trade simply because it's taking too long to play out, even if my stop hasn't been hit

price and time both matter when deciding whether a trade is still worth taking

builders.name: Polkadot
builders.bio: Products for People.

tweets.text:
At @web3summit 2026, people bought coffee, explored apps and deployed smart contracts. Several temporary networks supported those activities, but most attendees did not need to know which chain handled each task.

In its article, @paritytech connects that experience to the thinking behind Polkadot Products.

The approach addresses practical questions:

• Why should every developer rebuild the same tools? Shared services for identity, signing and payments can reduce the work needed before a team can focus on its application.
• Can apps feel more consistent across devices? Trinity explores a shared environment for mobile, desktop and the web, with applications using a common interface for those services.
• Does recognising a person require knowing who they are? Humanity focuses on establishing that someone is a unique person without revealing their identity.
• How easily can someone test an idea? At the Summit, Playground let participants modify working prototypes and deploy them to a temporary network.
The article describes work in progress, not a finished platform. It also acknowledges that getting started still needs to become easier for new users.
For technology built around people, ease of use is only part of the goal. The harder question is whether we can make software simpler without asking people to give up privacy, ownership or choice.

Less complexity should mean products that give people greater agency rather than platforms greater control.

Read the full article here: https://t.co/El95OKPPnb
